judgements.reason: Thesis (3rd platform ships inline MCP-channel policy enforcement as GA default by Q1 2027) is forward-looking with an 8+-month window (target 2027-01..2027-03) and stayed intact this week. The two anchoring data points (Zscaler AI Broker 6/9, Databricks Agent Bricks 6/16) are unchanged, and this week's developments reinforce the same move-the-control-point-into-the-runtime axis (Hermes MCP credential filtering/default-off gating, AWS Context runtime access control). No contradicting evidence to the because/given preconditions emerged.

Bridge set is healthy. 6/23 (rel=4, support=because) and 6/20-6/21 (rel=3, support=given) actively reinforce the reasoning preconditions. The latest 6/26 bridge (rel=1, support=none) correctly records that the Feast RCE is a feature-store deserialization flaw, not an MCP-channel issue, and does NOT advance the thesis -- this is an honest no-op record, not a contradict signal, so it does not invalidate reasoning. The relevance_drift trigger most likely fired on that single low-relevance day amid otherwise strong support; no bridge carries support_direction=contradict.

All three Needs (security PM shipping inline enforcement, enterprise architect creating pull demand, analyst/standards body codifying the pattern) remain open and forward-looking. No actor has delivered the named outcome -- a third major platform shipping production-ready inline MCP-channel access control as a documented GA default. Hermes and AWS Context reinforce the direction but are not the third-platform GA, so no Need status flips to done this week.

No new prediction_chain or prediction_relations edges surfaced for this prediction this week, and none of the upstream/equivalent landings or contradictions that would shorten or weaken the reasoning chain occurred. The thesis is fed by independent cross-platform signals rather than a single chained upstream, so the landing window is unaffected.
